title: Pinellia ternata lectin induces inflammation through TLR4 receptor and mediates PI3K/Akt/mTOR axis to regulate NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Li, Jinfei; Wang, Wei; Yuan, Yuan; Cui, Xiaobing; Bian, Huimin; Wen, Hongmei; Zhang, Xingde; Yu, Hongli; Wu, Hao
one_liner_zh: 该文研究半夏凝集素通过TLR4激活PI3K/Akt/mTOR和NF-κB通路诱导炎症，涉及蛋白-蛋白对接而非蛋白-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Pinellia ternata, a widely used traditional Chinese medicine, contains a strong mucosal irritant that is connected with Pinellia ternata lectin (PTL) in its tubers. The purpose of this study was to explore the mechanisms by which PTL induces inflammation. We found that in RAW264.7 cells, PTL activated the PI3K/Akt/mTOR and NF-kappaB pathways, which resulted in the release of proinflammatory cytokines. Flow cytometry and laser confocal microscopy analysis showed that FITC-labeled PTL bound to the macrophages' surface. Based on kinetic analyses and protein-protein docking simulations, PTL was shown to bind toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4).it was demonstrated that PTL binds highly to Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4). TLR4 knock-down or knockout resulted in a decrease in both cytokine release and PI3K/Akt/mTOR and NF-kappaB pathway activation in PTL-stimulated macrophages or mice. RNA-seq analysis showed that genes involved in the PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway were strongly upregulated in response to PTL stimulation, confirming that the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway is linked to the inflammatory effect of PTL in RAW264.7 cells. These findings reveal that PTL can mediate inflammation through TLR4 and activating the PI3K/Akt/mTOR to regulate NF-kappaB signaling pathways.
abstract_zh: 半夏（Pinellia ternata）作为一种广泛使用的中药材，其块茎中含有与半夏凝集素（PTL）相关的强黏膜刺激物。本研究旨在探讨PTL诱导炎症的机制。我们发现，在RAW264.7细胞中，PTL激活了PI3K/Akt/mTOR和NF-kappaB通路，从而导致促炎细胞因子的释放。流式细胞术和激光共聚焦显微镜分析显示，FITC标记的PTL结合于巨噬细胞表面。基于动力学分析和蛋白质-蛋白质对接模拟，PTL被证明能与Toll样受体4（TLR4）结合。研究表明，PTL与Toll样受体4（TLR4）具有高度结合性。在PTL刺激的巨噬细胞或小鼠中，TLR4敲低或敲除导致细胞因子释放减少，以及PI3K/Akt/mTOR和NF-kappaB通路激活降低。RNA-seq分析显示，响应PTL刺激时，参与PI3K/Akt/mTOR信号通路的基因显著上调，证实PI3K/Akt/mTOR通路与PTL在RAW264.7细胞中的炎症效应相关。这些发现揭示，PTL可通过TLR4介导炎症，并激活PI3K/Akt/mTOR以调节NF-kappaB信号通路。
